title: Rivelya
role: Solo full-stack developer: product, frontend, backend, infrastructure & DevOps
tagline: A pay-per-minute expert consultation marketplace with live chat, voice and video.
summary: An Italian marketplace where clients top up a wallet and consult verified experts by chat, voice or video, billed by the minute, booked ahead or started on demand.
challenge: Minute-based consultations are a high-volume, trust-sensitive business. The client needed a platform that could match clients with available experts instantly, meter every session precisely, collect payment upfront, hold and settle expert earnings and do all of it reliably in real time, without anyone reconciling balances by hand.
solution: I built Rivelya from scratch as a one-developer product: a React app for clients, experts and admins; an Express and Socket.io backend; self-hosted LiveKit for WebRTC voice and video; and a billing engine on MongoDB transactions that the server controls. The server starts, meters and closes every session, so the money is always right, even when a browser tab isn't.

highlights.title: Instant or scheduled sessions
highlights.text: Expert presence updates live. Clients can start a session immediately (the expert has 30 seconds to accept) or book a slot from the expert's availability calendar. A scheduler auto-starts booked sessions on time, in the Europe/Rome timezone.
highlights.alt: Rivelya expert directory with online status, ratings and channels

highlights.title: Chat, voice and video in one place
highlights.text: Socket.io powers chat, typing indicators, presence and call signalling. Voice and video run on a self-hosted LiveKit server with a TURN relay, with Twilio as a phone fallback. A live countdown shows each client exactly how much time is left.
highlights.alt: Rivelya expert profile with Start now button, reviews and channel options

highlights.title: Wallet and per-minute billing that can't drift
highlights.text: Stripe Payment Intents with verified webhooks top up a prepaid wallet held in integer cents. Every balance change runs in an atomic MongoDB transaction with idempotent payment handling, and negative balances are blocked. Expert earnings sit on a 7-day hold before they become withdrawable.
highlights.alt: Rivelya booking management showing a confirmed €19 session

highlights.title: Expert and admin consoles
highlights.text: Invite-only expert onboarding with availability, rates, earnings and withdrawal requests. The admin console has an OTP login and covers commission per expert, payouts, CMS and blog, testimonials and promotional email campaigns.
highlights.alt: Rivelya live session room with conversation list and timer

items: React SPA for clients, experts and admins

engineering: The server is the source of truth for billing: cron jobs start, meter and end sessions, and timers in the browser are display-only.
Payments are protected against duplicates with a unique index on the payment intent, a check before processing and atomic transactions.
Security: Helmet headers, rate limiting, verified Stripe webhooks, OTP admin sessions, KYC middleware and no direct S3 URLs.
GDPR: cookie consent, account deletion with OTP confirmation, and media served through an authenticated proxy with WebP conversion.
Push-to-deploy CI/CD with GitHub Actions: SSH, install, build and restart PM2 with no downtime.
Built-in AI support assistant using Groq Llama 3.1, with Gemini as a fallback.

title: Cover Me Lien Services
role: Solo full-stack developer: UX, frontend, backend, infrastructure & DevOps
tagline: A lien-compliance platform that helps California contractors protect their right to get paid.
summary: Construction-lien document preparation and deadline tracking for contractors, subcontractors, suppliers and law firms, with online intake, payments, a client portal and an admin back office.
coverAlt: Cover Me Lien Services homepage hero
challenge: In California construction, one missed statutory deadline can cost a contractor their lien rights, and the payment that comes with them. The client was taking orders by phone and email, working out deadlines by hand and chasing documents across inboxes. They needed a compliant self-service platform that could quote, take payment and collect documents, and give their team one place to run every case.
solution: I designed and built the whole product. It has a Next.js marketing site with California lien-law resources and a free deadline calculator, plus a multi-step intake with server-side pricing and Stripe Checkout. Clients get a secure portal for uploads and requests, and the team gets an admin back office to run each case. It's all deployed on a hardened Linux server with automated CI/CD.

highlights.title: Free deadline calculator
highlights.text: Five quick questions give state-specific lien deadlines in under a minute. The engine applies the earliest rule that matches and skips weekends. It's also the site's strongest lead magnet.
highlights.alt: Deadline calculator with five steps: state, project type, role, who hired you and last day on job

highlights.title: Guided intake and Stripe checkout
highlights.text: A three-step intake covers the request, the project and the signature. Pricing is calculated on the server (self-service vs full-service, plus a rush option) and paid through Stripe Checkout with signed, idempotent webhooks. Clients can resume an unpaid request at any time.
highlights.alt: Intake form with service selection, service levels and secure checkout summary

highlights.title: Secure client portal
highlights.text: Clients track every request, answer document and signature requests, and upload files straight to private, encrypted storage through presigned URLs. Each upload is checked with a checksum and verified by its file signature.
highlights.alt: Client request center showing request totals, actions needed and membership status

highlights.title: Attorney partner programme
highlights.text: A dedicated area for construction-law firms, with partnership packages and an inquiry pipeline, so attorneys can outsource lien paperwork with confidence.
highlights.alt: Attorney partnerships page: reliable, construction-focused lien support for law firms

engineering: JWT in httpOnly cookies with role-based access for clients and admins.
Per-route rate limits, NoSQL-injection and HTTP parameter pollution protection, and an exact-match CORS allowlist.
Uploads are SHA-256 checksummed and verified by file signature (magic bytes). Downloads use 60-second signed URLs, issued only after an ownership check.
Stripe webhooks are signature-verified and deduplicated through a stored event log.
SMS consent is stored separately from service terms, with a full audit history, and the site carries clear legal disclaimers that it is not a law firm (UPL compliance).
SEO: canonical URLs, Open Graph, JSON-LD and a generated sitemap. The CI/CD pipeline checks environment values before every deploy.

title: Tenant Certification
role: Lead & sole developer: took over a legacy platform; modernization, new features, payments & infrastructure
tagline: A national certification platform that turns renters into verified, trusted tenants.
summary: Training, verified records and a portable digital credential that help tenants prove they're ready, and help landlords, relocation teams and lenders trust them.
coverAlt: Tenant Certification homepage: the national standard for tenant and landlord excellence
challenge: Landlords judge applicants on little more than a credit score, and good renters have no way to prove they're prepared. Stellar Properties had the idea of certifying tenants through training and verified records, but their platform was ageing and had been built by earlier teams. They needed one developer to own it: stabilise and modernise it, connect payments and course delivery, and keep it running in production.
solution: I took over the codebase in October 2025 and have shipped 440+ commits since, as its only developer. That work includes a redesigned marketing site, a paid-access flow with verified Stripe webhooks and automatic certificate and wallet-card issuance when a course is completed. It also covers the tenant Credibility Kit and Timeline, an admin payment-review queue, security hardening and a push-to-deploy CI/CD pipeline.

highlights.title: Certification academy
highlights.text: A structured course path covering budgeting, credibility, legal basics, maintenance and rental search. CustomerHub delivers the courses, and its completion webhook (protected with a constant-time token check) triggers certification automatically.
highlights.alt: Courses to complete for certification: introduction, credibility kit, budgeting, legal, maintenance and more

highlights.title: The Stellar Credential
highlights.text: Graduates receive a digital certificate and wallet card issued through the Certifier API. A built-in diagnostics self-test and a retry path make sure no certificate is ever lost.
highlights.alt: Certificate of Stewardship and wallet card: stop being a risk and start being a result

highlights.title: Credibility Kit and Rental Passport
highlights.text: Tenants build a verified Credibility Kit: documents uploaded to private object storage (with size limits and scanning), a rental Timeline, references and reports. All of it can be shared as a single Rental Passport.
highlights.alt: Train, verify, connect: the three steps of the certification journey

highlights.title: Payments and access control
highlights.text: Stripe webhooks are verified by hand with HMAC-SHA256 and processed exactly once. Refunds and disputes suspend access automatically, and payments that can't be matched go to an admin review queue instead of getting lost.
highlights.alt: Choose your version: professional steward, Stellar landlord or corporate relocator

items: Vue SPA for tenants, landlords, organisations and admins

engineering: Took over a 2021 codebase and modernized it while it stayed live, with no big-bang rewrite.
Stripe signatures are verified by hand with timingSafeEqual, and events are stored idempotently in a dedicated table.
A self-test endpoint checks CustomerHub, Certifier and the database without writing anything, which makes production issues quick to diagnose.
Hardening: strict CORS allowlist, CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, an allowlist of document hosts and a size cap on downloads.
Tightened password handling so profile edits never store blank or plain-text passwords.
One-push deploys: GitHub Actions builds both apps, runs migrations, restarts PM2 and reloads Nginx.

title: Grand Hotel Selinunte
role: Full-stack developer: website, AI guest support & internal tools
tagline: Hotel website, AI guest-support chat with WhatsApp, and internal finance tools.
summary: The official website of a seafront hotel in Sicily, plus an AI chat assistant that answers guests on the web and WhatsApp, and in-house tools that automate quotes and receipts.
challenge: An international hotel gets the same guest questions all day, in several languages, across the website and WhatsApp, while the front office was still building quotes and receipts by hand. The hotel needed a modern website that converts, round-the-clock answers for guests and less manual admin work.
solution: I built and deployed the official website with a custom React frontend and a fully responsive booking journey. I then added an AI chat support system connected to WhatsApp for multilingual guest questions, plus internal tools that generate PDF quotes and receipts and calculate stay costs automatically.

highlights.title: Website and booking journey
highlights.text: A fast, fully responsive website with a custom React frontend, designed to turn visitors into direct bookings. It's deployed on AWS behind Nginx with SSL.
highlights.alt: Rooms with a view and Sicilian dining sections of the hotel website

highlights.title: AI chat support with WhatsApp
highlights.text: An AI assistant answers guest questions about rooms, services and bookings in several languages, on the website and over WhatsApp, around the clock.

highlights.title: Internal finance tools
highlights.text: A cost calculator, a PDF quote generator and a receipt generator. Together they cut manual formatting and speed up replies to guests.

engineering: Production deployment on AWS virtual machines behind Nginx with SSL.
Responsive, SEO-friendly pages built for hospitality search terms.
AI assistant tuned to the hotel's own information, available on the web and on WhatsApp.
